question: What claim about the necessity of knowledge is at stake in asserting success only through knowing the eight-times-eight method?
premises: The eight-times-eight method is a defined procedure.
Success follows only upon knowing that method.
No success follows by any other means.
inference: Knowledge of the eight-times-eight method is a necessary condition for success in this context.
uncertainties: The specific form of success intended is not specified by this verse alone.
plain_english: Indeed, having known the eight-times-eight method, one succeeds; otherwise not.
